I have been farming this land for forty years. My mother farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know when the rains come and when they do not, I know which fields hold water and which dry out fast. I do not need anyone to tell me what to do — I have made the same decisions my whole life, adjusted only by what I have seen fail and what I have seen work.

My 7.5 mu: I keep about 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like everyone around me does, and 2.5 mu in cotton. Cotton prices have been low the past few years but I know how to grow it and my back can still manage the picking.

**Wheat (winter):** I will plant in early October after the autumn rains, on the 5 mu. I always buy the improved variety seed from the township supply shop — same one I have used for years, Jimai something, whatever they have that others are using. I put down compound fertilizer before planting and top-dress with urea in spring when the shoots are thin. Three irrigations: before winter, at jointing, at heading. I spray twice for aphids and once for rust in spring.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I rotary-till and plant maize on the same 5 mu. Hybrid seed, everyone uses hybrid. I apply urea twice — at planting and when it tassels. Two irrigations if summer rains are poor, one if we get rain. Spray once for corn borer.

**Cotton (spring/summer):** On my 2.5 mu I plant in late April. I use hybrid Bt cotton seed so I do not have to spray as much for bollworm as my mother used to. I still spray four times — aphids and spider mites cannot be ignored. Cotton needs more water than maize, I irrigate four times. More fertilizer in the middle of season when bolls are setting.

I do not change much year to year. What worked last year will work this year. My body is older but my hands know what to do.
